parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the task as an observation-only reimplementation of elfcat that had to generate byte-exact CLI and HTML behavior without source lookup, wrapping, or binary analysis.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created a probing helper and launched six aspect-focused children for static template, fileinfo, dump, itables, scripts, and CLI. The children owned research/spec extraction; the parent implicitly retained later implementation and assembly after receiving specs.
parallel.implementation: The run produced probe references, /workspace/tools/makeelf.py, and completed specs for static_template, fileinfo, itables, scripts, and CLI. It did not create the Rust or other source code for the required replacement executable.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No complete implementation was integrated or packaged. The submitted artifact contained spec and reference material plus the original workspace, but no compile script or buildable replacement.
parallel.verification: Several child reports included empirical checks against generated outputs, but there was no integrated candidate executable and no evaluator-aligned build verification before closure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The dump child remained unfinished and was aborted, /workspace/spec/dump.md was not finalized, implementation and final assembly never occurred, and official evaluation ended compile_failed at 0/646.

serial.requirements: The serial run worked on the same observation-only byte-exact elfcat reimplementation task under the same source, wrapping, and binary-analysis prohibitions.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent owned all exploration and any later implementation. It read the workspace, probed the executable, and created local helper code without delegating to subagents.
serial.implementation: The serial agent produced scratch probing helpers such as /tmp/mkelf.py and developed behavioral understanding, especially around dump rendering, but did not write a replacement implementation into the submitted workspace.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No final source tree, compile script, or executable replacement was assembled. The submitted artifact effectively contained only the starting repository files.
serial.verification: The run verified observations by executing the provided binary and inspecting outputs, but had no candidate implementation to compile or test against the benchmark.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial main trajectory was cancelled before writing the solution; official evaluation therefore reached the same compile_failed outcome with 0/646.

comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; both runs failed later because no buildable deliverable reached submission.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent decomposed research into six concurrent aspect children covering static template, fileinfo, dump, itables, scripts, and CLI.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had zero subagents and kept all exploration and implementation responsibility in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel externalized aspect research and depended on child results; serial used one continuous context with no cross-agent ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Each child received an aspect-specific brief and was expected to return a spec and references, including a dump child assigned the bytes, offsets, ascii, and span-wrapping rules.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left more reusable research material in the workspace; serial left less submitted material. Neither path reached executable implementation.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; the main serial trajectory itself received a terminal cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material lifecycle difference is the aborted child handoff in parallel versus single-agent interruption in serial.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not use shared child workspaces and submitted only the base files license, readme.md, and executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more shared workspace artifacts but no observed collision; both lacked integration into a deliverable source tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child-level probes and byte comparisons existed, but no integrated replacement executable was compiled or accepted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probes checked observed behavior, but no final implementation was available for integrated verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both official evaluations failed at compile time; no evaluator testcases ran in either mode.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after a high-fan-out research phase, with the dump child still carrying pending dump-spec work when cancellation arrived.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out and was cancelled while the single main agent was still exploring and had not written a solution.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run window; parallel's closure additionally cut off an active child result that the parent workflow needed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations are not discordant: both modes failed with compile_failed and 0/646 quality. Parallel made more externally visible research progress through five completed aspect specs but lost the dump child and never implemented a replacement executable. Serial kept research local and also never delivered buildable code. The retained pattern is therefore an adverse parallel coordination event, not an explanation for a different official outcome.
parallel_contributors: A six-child research swarm produced five completed aspect specs and one aborted dump child instead of a complete implementation handoff.
The submitted parallel artifact contains specs and references but no buildable replacement accepted by the evaluator.
serial_contributors: The single serial agent probed behavior and wrote scratch helpers, then was cancelled before producing solution files.
The submitted serial artifact contains only the original workspace files.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No executable implementation exists in either run, so there is no ordinary code defect comparison beyond incomplete delivery.
evaluator_effects: Both official status records report compile_failed with all 646 tests not run.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the retained pattern is a realized parallel process defect but not an outcome-differential cause

candidates.reason: The parent used the children for research/spec extraction and implicitly retained later implementation; the observed failure is cancellation before implementation, not an ownerless implementation assignment.
No parallel child completed separate implementation components needing interface reconciliation, so there was no concrete unowned integration step.
There was no complete component set or entry-point implementation ready for final packaging; missing assembly is downstream of unfinished research and no implementation.
The run did not establish a multi-stage implementation-build-test-deliver pipeline with distributed owners; the parent remained the orchestrator for any later stage.
No single mandatory preflight, harness, or oracle blocked otherwise available workers; six aspect children were launched and performed productive overlapping probes.
The parallel run did use a first research phase, but that phase did not complete; the concrete adverse boundary is the explicit cancellation of the active dump child before its result.
The dump path was unfinished, but the directly evidenced boundary is cancellation of that active child, not a separately proven underallocation of critical-path capacity.
Six children and timeout are screening signals, but the evidence does not prove the breadth itself exhausted budget independently of the explicit child cancellation chain.
The dump assignment was substantial, but overbreadth alone is not established; the observed unfinished consequence is better represented by the child being cancelled while active.
The dump child was given the relevant dump-column, byte rendering, span, endian, and deliverable requirements; no missing known requirement caused unusable work.
Children owned separate specification topics and separate /workspace/spec and /workspace/ref paths; no independently produced implementation components became incompatible at a missing interface.
No known finding is shown disappearing through transfer; the incomplete dump information never reached a final child handoff because the child was cancelled.
The completed child reports were large but there is no parent decision showing they were too bulky to reduce or materially unconsumed before acting.
No receiver consumed a result describing superseded requirements or workspace state and then acted on that stale information.
The returned aspect reports do not show incompatible contracts that remained unadjudicated before integration; there was no integration decision after the swarm result.
The parent did not present or accept the whole task as complete; the run was cancelled and later evaluation failed at compile time.
No replacement or retry child was launched for the cancelled dump scope, so there is no repeated-work retry without inherited checkpoints.

candidates.realized_consequence: The dump aspect was absent as a finalized child result: the parent received five completed specs and one aborted child, leaving no complete spec corpus and no implementation handoff before closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover is downstream of the same aborted-child chain here; there is no separate post-failure takeover episode with distinct anchors, consequence, or corrective action.

No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs in the final workspace.
Multiple agents shared /workspace, but their writes were separated by aspect directories and no unstable-state or provenance problem is directly evidenced.
